title: Missing Connection Keepalive / Idle Timeout on Long-lived Sockets
pattern: Reusing or holding persistent connection handles (such as database or network streams) in a pool or struct without configuring TCP keepalives (`set_nodelay`, `set_keepalive`) or an idle connection eviction timeout.
why_bad: Stateful network devices, such as firewalls and routers, maintain finite connection state tables [595]. If a socket sits idle for a long duration, the firewall silently evicts it from its tables [595]. Because TCP does not notify endpoints of this eviction, subsequent attempts to read/write from the socket will block indefinitely as the TCP stack endlessly retries packet transmissions against a silent firewall, hanging the calling thread [595, 597].
detection: Identify socket or pool configurations that do not set TCP keepalives or idle timeout connection recycling.
fix: Enable TCP keepalive options on sockets, and configure connection pools to recycle/validate idle connections that exceed firewalls' inactivity limits [597, 232].
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 2 & Chapter 10 (Pool Connections) / passages [595, 597, 232].
